DHADDHA Judgment Date of judgment 19/05/2023

The present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants-claimants (for short 'the claimants')
dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 27.6.2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.1, Jaipur Metropolitan Jaipur (for short 'the Tribunal') in MAC No.377/2014 whereby the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.4,90,000/- along with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of filing the claim petition in favour of the claimants on account of death of Smt. Sona in the accident took place on 24.2.2014.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.1, Jaipur Metropolitan Jaipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Tribunal on the basis of the pleading of the parties, framed the issues and evaluated the evidence on record.
After hearing counsel for the parties, decided the claim petition of the claimants and awarded the amount as indicated above.
Feeling dissatisfied with the impugned award, claimants have filed the instant appeal inter-alia on the various grounds.
Learned counsel for the claimants submits that tribunal wrongly considered the income of the deceased Rs.4,000/- per month.
He also submits that deceased was doing household business and earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
He also submits that at the time of accident, minimum wages of unskilled labour was Rs.189 per day.
So, income of the deceased be modified accordingly and the same should be Rs.5670/- per month.
He further submits that tribunal wrongly deducted 1/2 personal expenses of the deceased whereas looking to the number of dependents it should be 1/4 of the deceased's income.
He also [2023/RJJP/011128] (3 of 4) [CMA-4939/2018] submits that tribunal awarded Rs.40,000/- lumpsum as loss of love and consortium whereas it should be Rs.40,000/- per person.
So, award of the tribunal be modified accordingly.
Learned counsel for the respondents submits that claimants had not submitted any cogent evidence that deceased Smt. Sona Devi was earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
So, tribunal rightly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.4,000/- per month.
Learned tribunal deducted 1/2 as personal expenses of the deceased because appellants No.2 to 5 are major and they are not dependent upon the deceased.
He also submits that tribunal rightly awarded amount Rs.40,000/- lumpsum as loss of love and affection.
So, appeal be dismissed.
I have considered the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the claimants as well as respondents.
It is an admitted position that claimants had not submitted any cogent evidence that deceased was earning Rs.12,000/- per month by doing household business.
In my considered opinion, tribunal wrongly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.4,000/- per month because minimum wages Act at that time were Rs.189 per day.
Tribunal wrongly deducted 1/2 amount towards personal expenses of the deceased whereas it should be 1/4.
Learned tribunal wrongly awarded Rs.40,000/- lumpsum towards love and affection whereas it should be Rs.40,000/- for each claimants.

So, judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent as under:-
Annual Income Rs.189X30X12=68040

Since, claimant was 43 years of Rs.63787X14=893018 age at the time of accident, multiplier of 14 should be applied Love and affection Rs.40,000/- Rs.40,000X6=2,40,000/-
 to each claimants
Loss of estate Rs.15
Funeral expesnes Rs.15

Total compensation awarded  Rs.11  Less amount awarded by the  Tribunal Rs.4,90,000/-
 Enhanced amount of  compensation Rs.6,
In view of the above, the claimants-appellants are entitled to get a sum of Rs.11,63,018/- as compensation.

Insurance Company is directed to deposit enhanced amount of Rs. Rs.6,73,018/-
(Rs.11,63,018-Rs.4,90,000) with the Tribunal within a period of two months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
On deposition of the said amount, the claimants shall be entitled to withdrawn the same.
The enhanced amount shall carry 7% interest from the date of filing of claim petition till the actual payment is made.
Consequently, the appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned judgment and award is modified accordingly.
Rest part of the impugned judgment and award shall remain unchanged.
Pending application(s), if any, also stand(s) disposed of.
